clues: This city in the north of Brazil is a port on a wide river. It sits a short way up that river from the Atlantic Ocean, at the gate to a great rain forest.
Rain falls here in all twelve months, so there is no true dry time of year. The wettest months run from December to May, when rains come most days.
This town was set up in 1616 by men from Portugal. It was the first town from Europe on the great river.
Locals call this place the city of mango trees. That is because mango trees grow all over, in its streets, squares, and yards.
The old part of town keeps its charm, with tree-filled squares and old churches. Many old homes there wear blue tiles, a mark of the old days.
